reason: The hypothesis relies on the premise that interfaces block dislocations and reduce creep, but the cited evidence does not directly support this for the proposed HfNbTaTiZr multilayer system. E1 describes shear band formation in a bulk HfNbTaTiZr HEA without interfaces, E2 discusses γ/γ′ interfaces in a different HESA system, and E3 shows slow dislocation motion in a bulk HEA without engineered interfaces. None of the cited passages provide evidence for the key premises regarding engineered multilayer interfaces in refractory HEAs.
premises: Interfaces in HEAs can block dislocation motion
Lattice mismatch and chemical heterogeneity at interfaces generate internal stress fields that impede dislocations
Dislocation blocking at interfaces reduces time-dependent plastic deformation (creep)
Multilayer HEA coatings can be fabricated with controlled lattice mismatch and sharp interfaces at 10-20 nm thickness
Dislocation pile-ups and locked networks at interfaces are observable by TEM and correlate with reduced creep
